rules.name: Additional Course Requirements
rules.desc:
PhD students in Biophysics must also complete at least four additional graduate-level courses in physical or biological sciences, which must include:
at least 1 literature-based course in biological science, and
at least 1 quantitative course in physical science.
Suggested courses for fulfilling these requirements are listed in detail below.

rules.name: Qualifying Exam
rules.desc: PhD students in Biophysics are required to complete a qualifying exam by the end of the second year. This exam consists of a written proposal for dissertation research, and an oral defense of the proposal. The examiners consist of the student’s prospective thesis reading committee, including the thesis advisor and typically two additional Stanford faculty members. The committee will determine if the student is prepared to conduct the thesis research, and may award an unconditional pass, a pass with conditions specified by the committee, or a fail. Additional details are provided in the Student Handbook.

rules.name: Teaching
rules.desc: Although teaching is not a requirement for the degree, students may teach as part of the financial support commitment and their professional training.

rules.name: Research
rules.desc: During the first year, students conduct up to three research rotations in prospective thesis laboratories, with each rotation lasting one quarter. A fourth rotation during the summer may be approved by the Program Director in exceptional cases. As a requirement of the program, students are expected to match with a thesis advisor by the end of the first year, and conduct thesis research for the remainder of the PhD program.

rules.name: Candidacy
rules.desc: Admission to candidacy is a prospective judgement by the faculty of a student’s potential to successfully complete the requirements of the degree program. Qualifying procedures in Biophysics include required coursework, research rotations, identification of an advisor, and successful completion of the Qualifying Exam.

rules.name: University Oral Exam
rules.desc: In the Biophysics Program, the oral exam is a defense of the dissertation presented upon the completion of a pre-final draft. Students consult with their dissertation advisor and reading committee members on the timing of the defense. Students are expected to complete this milestone by the end of their sixth year in the program.

rules.name: Dissertation Requirement
rules.desc: Students are required to submit an approved dissertation that makes an original contribution to scientific knowledge in the field of Biophysics. Students are expected to submit the dissertation in the same quarter that they complete the oral exam, and no later than the subsequent quarter.
